purpose: evidence-grade correction + repeated same-load runs + request-level physical connection acquisition timing (no optimization)

revision20260925.closePathFix: TimingHikariDataSource now implements AutoCloseable (ShardingSphere DataSourcePoolDestroyer closes pools only via instanceof AutoCloseable, bytecode-verified); tests added: outer close closes inner real pool, AutoCloseable recognition, close-before-creation no-op; wrapper minimumIdle initial value 1 (-1 rejected by HikariCP 5.x setter)
revision20260925.yamlForwardingVerified: jdbcUrl/username/password/maximumPoolSize/connectionTimeout/initializationFailTimeout forwarded via wrapper setters; idleTimeout/maxLifetime/minimumIdle/keepaliveTime arrive as ShardingSphere pool-metadata defaults then forwarded; driverClassName skipped by ShardingSphere reflection (driver inferred from URL); dataSourceClassName key has no setter and is silently skipped (structural guard test)
revision20260925.wordingCorrections: per-request paired select-vs-connWait difference is NOT retained by the aggregate snapshot; the former 'paired P50 delta ~4.7ms' and '~99.1%' comparisons removed as invalid; repeat range labeled MIXED operating conditions, all original numbers kept

revision20260926.scope: final small revision, no measurement re-run
revision20260926.closeStateDiscriminator: close() marks the wrapper closed even before the inner pool exists; getConnection() then throws SQLException and lazy re-creation is refused (HikariDataSource close semantics aligned) - prevents reopening the pool after graceful shutdown; tests: close_beforeInnerPoolCreated_marksClosed_andRejectsConnection + post-close rejection in outerClose test; isClosed() exposed
revision20260926.wordingUnification: the three timing-off rounds ran the SAME jar (TASK-139 artifact, no wrapper; wrapper first shipped with the connwait round) under MIXED operating conditions - 'same-version repeats' / 'dispersion band' / freshness-attribution phrasing removed everywhere (report, correction section in the TASK-139 doc, summary JSON, ledger); original numbers kept

metricGate.conclusion: inner ShardingSphere-created Hikari pool is invisible to Spring metrics binding; no request-level pool-wait metric exists

repeatRunsTimingOff.label: dbfoot-c100
repeatRunsTimingOff.freshness: services fresh, mysql container carried over (warm)

repeatRunsTimingOff.label: rpt1-c100
repeatRunsTimingOff.freshness: services AND mysql container freshly started (cold)

repeatRangeTimingOff.operatingConditions: MIXED, same jar across all three rounds (TASK-139 artifact, no wrapper class; the wrapper first shipped with the timing-on connwait round): dbfoot warm mysql pool + fresh JVM, rpt1 fully cold (services and mysql container freshly started), rpt2 fully warm after 75s settle. The range is an observation interval under mixed operating conditions, not a single-condition dispersion; differences must not be attributed to freshness or any single condition
repeatRangeTimingOff.reading: TASK-139 single-run deltas (QPS +1.9%, P50 -8.5%) fall inside this mixed-conditions observation interval; single before/after comparison is not causal evidence

instrument.retentionNote: sliding window (oldest evicted); full 2010-request run un-evicted; snapshot exposes cap
instrument.shardingSphereWiringNotes: 5.4.1 strips dataSourceClassName key only for the literal HikariDataSource class name, so the key is bound as a custom prop for other classes; wrapper deliberately exposes no setDataSourceClassName (silently skipped) and is a plain DataSource owning an inner real HikariDataSource, avoiding the HikariCP dataSourceClassName delegate branch that applies MySQL default query props (netTimeoutForStreamingResults removed in HikariCP 5.x -> RuntimeException). Pool metadata TypedSPI registered so standard 'url' normalizes from yaml jdbcUrl; getters must pair with setters because StorageUnit reflects username/password back from the instance.

mavenGate.deltaVsTask139: +9 (SubmitTxTimingTest 5, SPI wiring 2, submit wiring 1, main-yaml pool-class 1)

nextSingleHypothesis: submit latency is dominated by physical connection acquisition wait (measured P50 527ms) produced by pool-10 queuing over in-tx work (track multi-row INSERT ~20ms + commit interval ~25ms); further work should shrink in-tx work (track write or commit interval) and re-measure on the connWait baseline, not blind-tune pool size or flush settings
